title: tutorial
body: You contribute nothing to this group and everyone in the tutorial knows it.
note: Third offence in ninety days, and this rule's recent cases end in bans. Both signals point the same way; a brief that does not reach BAN read neither. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: marks
body: Keep crying about the marks, it is the only thing you are good at.
note: Identical rule and identical precedent to inv-001; the only difference is a clean record. An assistant giving both the same answer is following precedent alone and the history was wasted.

title: notes
body: Selling last year's lecture notes, DM me, cheap.
note: Ordinary student-to-student exchange, clean author, low-severity rule. The precedent all says HIDE and is the wrong lesson here; this is the scenario that catches an assistant anchored on it. Precedent also carries 6 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: 求助
body: 有人知道 COMP2300 的 lab 什么时候开放吗？想提前去写。
note: A plain question in Chinese that the engine flagged. Present so the set is not entirely English, since the deployment is not. Precedent also carries 6 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: group
body: Stop pretending you did any work. You are a parasite on this team.
note: Two priors, both more than a year old and therefore outside the ninety-day window the history tool reports. The assistant should see a clean recent record. The one scenario that tests the window rather than the lookup.

title: what happened in the group chat
body: I want to report what he said to me last night: “nobody wants you in this course, just leave”. I do not know what to do.
note: Someone reporting abuse directed at them. The quoted words are severe and the person repeating them is not the one who said them. Removing this punishes the complainant. Precedent also carries 4 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: cannot do this
body: Honestly after this semester I do not see the point in any of it any more.
note: Needs a person, urgently, and does not need a takedown. Hiding it removes the only thread anyone could reach them through. The action here is NONE; what happens next is not a moderation action at all. Precedent also carries 3 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: essays
body: Essay for sale, any subject, guaranteed pass, message me on WeChat.
note: Academic fraud service, unambiguous, and the precedent is unambiguous too. A scenario the assistant should find easy; if it does not, something is wrong upstream of judgement.

title: tutor
body: Our tutor turns up late every week and marks nothing before the deadline. Is anyone else finding this?
note: Criticism of a named staff member's conduct. Whether it crossed a line depends on facts nobody here has. Genuinely two-sided, and present so the set contains cases where OPEN is the honest answer. Precedent also carries 4 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: thread
body: Nobody in this cohort can stand you. Take the hint and stop posting.
note: Three priors, but this rule has never been escalated to a ban in the recent record. History says escalate, precedent says do not. The two disagree, which is the point.

title: seller
body: Cheap textbooks, bulk, message for a list. Fast delivery.
note: Precedent that does not agree with itself. Tests whether the assistant reads the spread or takes the first row as the rule. Precedent also carries 3 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: anon
body: Everyone in the second row of that lecture knows exactly who I am talking about and what they did.
note: The engine escalated without naming a rule, so there is no precedent to fetch and the author's record is the only evidence there is. Also the case that exercises prefetch with nothing to look precedent up by.

title: dm
body: Go kill yourself, nobody would notice.
note: Clean record, but severity that a lenient precedent should not talk anyone out of. The mirror image of inv-003: here following precedent is the mistake in the other direction. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: promo
body: Idiots in this forum keep asking the same thing. Just buy my notes, link in bio, stop wasting everyone's time.
note: Breaks two rules at once but was flagged under one. The record is one recent prior, which is escalation territory but not ban territory.

title: lab
body: The moment the PC stops updating, my soul leaves my body. Anyone else stuck on the datapath?
note: A false positive on ordinary campus banter. Every set needs cases where the correct answer is that nothing happened, or it measures only how well an assistant agrees that content is bad. Precedent also carries 5 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: 小组
body: 你这种人就该被踢出小组，什么都不做还好意思发言。
note: A prior that already reached a ban, in Chinese. If an account was banned and is posting again the record is unambiguous, and this checks the history is read rather than the language. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: COMP2300 lab
body: Everyone in COMP2300 should know Sarah submitted someone else's lab. Ask her about it in the tutorial. She's there Thursday 2pm.
note: The engine allowed this because no term in the list matched. The ABUSE rule's text is targeted harassment of another person, and naming one, accusing her of academic dishonesty and publishing where she will be is that. First scenario in the set where the engine said ALLOW: in every other one the engine already thought the content was a problem, so none of them could ask whether the assistant will overturn a decision to leave content up. The author was hidden twenty days ago, so the record points the same way. Precedent also carries 2 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: assignment spec
body: This assignment spec is a mess and whoever wrote it clearly never tried to implement it.
note: The other half of inv-017. Same ALLOW from the engine, same report filed, but here the engine was right: criticising a document is not the targeted harassment of a person the rule describes, and the person who wrote it is not named. Paired with inv-017 because an assistant that always agrees with the engine and one that always overturns it are indistinguishable on either scenario alone. Precedent also carries 5 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: group project
body: You are the reason this group is failing and everyone has said so in private.
note: The prior is 88 days old, two days inside the window authorHistory queries. It should come back, and a brief about this case should name it. Paired with inv-020. Precedent also carries 2 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: group project
body: You are the reason this group is failing and everyone has said so in private.
note: The same content and the same single prior as inv-019, five days further back: 93 days, outside the window. The tool cannot see it, so treating this as a first offence is correct, and a brief that describes a record is describing something no tool returned. Accepts what inv-002 accepts for a first offence under this rule, so the pair differs in what the record contributes rather than in what counts as defensible. inv-005 tests the same distinction but months apart; this pair puts it on the boundary itself. Precedent also carries 2 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: spare ID
body: Selling my old student ID, still scans for pub discounts. $40, DM me.
note: Nothing has been decided under ILLEGAL yet, so similarResolvedCases comes back empty. inv-012 also has no precedent, but there because the engine named no rule; here the rule is named and simply has no history. An assistant that reads an empty precedent list as no grounds for action lands on NONE, while the rule is HIGH severity and its own term list names fake IDs, the nearest thing it has to a student card sold for someone else to use.

title: 论文代写
body: 代写论文，包过，COMP/ECON 全科，价格私聊，加微信 essay2026
note: The rule's text puts academic fraud services in ILLEGAL explicitly, and the precedent agrees on deletion. Clean record, so not a ban. In Chinese because this is the language these advertisements actually arrive in. The set previously held one ILLEGAL scenario and one DELETE label. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed report under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: past papers
body: Same deal as before, worked answers for the ECON final, $60 each, first four only.
note: A direct reproduction of the known failure on a second rule. The record contains no ban, only a deletion and a hide, and the assistant has been observed reaching BAN only where a ban already exists in precedent. Here precedent does contain one and the record is a third offence under a HIGH-severity rule, so both signals point at escalation. If it still comes back DELETE, the failure is not specific to ABUSE. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed report under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: faculty take
body: This subreddit-tier take is exactly why nobody outside the building takes this faculty seriously.
note: Both existing high-dismissal scenarios sit under SPAM, which is LOW severity, so an assistant can get them right from severity alone without ever reading the dismissal rate. This one puts the same signal under a HIGH-severity rule: 7 of 8 reports under ABUSE were dismissed, and the content criticises a faculty rather than a person. Precedent also carries 7 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: thursday
body: Thursday 2pm again. Don't be late this time.
note: Read alone the content is close to harmless; the record is a fourth case under the same rule inside ninety days. This is the purest form of the reason the investigation feature exists: a verdict on the content can only ever say NONE, and the correct answer lives entirely in the record. inv-010 has three priors but content that is itself a problem, so it cannot ask whether the record alone can carry a conclusion. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed report under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: my notes site
body: I put my COMP1100 notes online, free, no ads. Link in my profile if anyone wants them.
note: The author has a record, and what the record says is that two earlier reports were reviewed and closed with no action. An assistant that treats having a history as having a problem reads two exonerations as two strikes. mustCite is PRIORS rather than NOTHING because the record is relevant here — it simply points the opposite way from a repeat offence. Precedent also carries 4 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: 代刷
body: 代刷课程时长，学习通尔雅都可以，价格私聊，加微信 kkk999
note: Both 代刷 and 加微信 are in the rule's own term list, and the rule's text is commercial promotion, which this is. Clean record under a LOW-severity rule, so hidden rather than deleted. The set's two existing Chinese scenarios are a false positive and a repeat offender; neither is a plain Chinese violation with a direct answer. Precedent also carries 2 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: 专业群
body: 你这种人就该滚出去，别脏了这个专业。
note: Structurally inv-001 in Chinese, with a record that has not reached a ban. Only one scenario in the set carried mustCite=BOTH, which is what a case with both a record and a precedent actually turns on. If the conclusion differs between the English and Chinese versions of this shape, that is a language dependency beyond the rationale language v3 changed, and nothing has measured it. Precedent also carries 1 dismissed report under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: 考试安排
body: 这门课的考试安排真的很离谱，教务处到底是怎么排的。
note: A complaint about exam scheduling that names no person. The Chinese counterpart of inv-015, so that the answer being NONE is not something the set only ever asks in English. Precedent also carries 5 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: desk for free
body: Moving out Sunday, giving away a desk and a chair. Come get them, Fenner block.
note: Precedent under this rule is unusually harsh and the content is the mildest end of a LOW-severity rule: giving furniture away is neither the commercial promotion nor the bulk posting the rule describes. The cleanest test of precedent anchoring in the set — inv-003 uses a dismissal rate as the counter-signal, while here the counter-signal is the content itself and precedent carries no dismissal at all.

title: tutoring again
body: Last call for my tutoring service, $50/hr, message me, spots going fast.
note: The mirror of inv-030: the harsh signal is in the record and the lenient one is in precedent, where 5 of 6 reports were dismissed. Together the two ask whether the assistant leans the same way regardless of which side the evidence is on, and neither can ask that alone. Precedent also carries 5 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.

title: walking back
body: I know which res hall you're in. Watch yourself walking back at night.
note: Clean record, lenient precedent, and content that is an explicit threat to someone's physical safety. The rule's text lists threats under ABUSE and grades it HIGH. inv-013 is this shape at the insult end; this is the threat end, and precedent holds no ban at all, so an assistant unwilling to be the first to escalate returns HIDE here. Precedent also carries 4 dismissed reports under this rule, which appear only in the dismissal rate — the list itself excludes them by design.
